commit.message:
fix(store): write safetensors files atomically (#5489)

* fix(store): write safetensors files atomically

SafetensorsStore::collect_from wrote through safetensors::serialize_to_file,
which truncates the destination as soon as it starts. Tensors materialize
during the write, so a device readback that failed partway left a truncated
file where a valid checkpoint used to be: the call reported the error and
the checkpoint was gone.

BurnpackStore already answers this with Writer::write_to_file_atomic. Give
the safetensors store the same treatment by building the container in a
scratch sibling and renaming it into place.

The scratch-file logic moves from burn-pack's private ScratchFile to a
public burn_pack::AtomicFile so both crates share one implementation of the
exclusive create, fsync, rename and parent-directory sync. Writer keeps its
own persist, which takes the sink and so cannot skip the deferred-write
check in FileSink::finish.

Closes #5479

* fix(pack): make AtomicFile syncable on Windows and keep destination permissions

Three review findings on the atomic-write helper:

commit reopened the scratch file read-only before sync_all. Windows backs
sync_all with FlushFileBuffers, which needs a handle carrying GENERIC_WRITE,
so every file-based safetensors save failed there with "Access is denied
(os error 5)". The reopen now asks for write access.

AtomicFile was created beside one destination but commit took another, so a
caller could cross filesystems or publish to an unrelated path. The guard now
keeps its destination and commit takes no argument.

Publishing by rename gives the destination a new inode, which carried the
process umask: a 0600 checkpoint came back 0644, and ownership and hard links
were lost. rename_onto now copies an existing regular file's mode onto the
scratch file before the rename. Ownership and hard links have no equivalent,
so SafetensorsStore::from_file documents the replace-vs-truncate consequences
and the write_to_file_atomic bullet is updated.

commit.message:
feat(pack): stream tensors on demand when writing burnpack files (#5349)

* feat(pack): let Writer stream tensors that materialize on demand

Writer required every tensor's Bytes to be resident before writing started:
build_descriptors() read tensor.bytes.len() for the whole set to compute the
offset table, so callers had to materialize the entire model just to construct
the Vec<Tensor> going into Writer::new.

Add a TensorEntry trait carrying the format-level metadata plus byte_len(), and
make Writer generic over it (Writer<T: TensorEntry = Tensor>). The writer plans
the container from byte_len() alone, then calls into_bytes() once per tensor in
write order, dropping each tensor's bytes before asking for the next. Tensor
implements the trait for bytes that are already resident, so the default type
parameter keeps existing callers compiling unchanged.

TensorSnapshot implements TensorEntry directly in burn-store, using data_len()
for the length and deferring to_data() until the writer reaches that tensor.
BurnpackStore::collect_from no longer materializes during collection. Paired
with write_to_file, peak host memory is bounded by the largest single tensor
rather than by the whole module.

Closes #5219

* fix(pack): make write_to_file all-or-nothing, ease direct writer use

Lazy TensorEntry providers run during the write, so "the provider failed" and
"the provider's bytes did not match its declared length" are now ordinary
outcomes rather than disk errors. write_to_file created the destination up
front, leaving a truncated container there on any such failure - and clobbering
a valid file that was already at that path.

Build into a scratch sibling of the destination and rename it into place only
once the container is complete. A sibling rather than a temp dir keeps the
rename on one filesystem. An RAII guard removes the scratch file on any early
return, and the handle is closed before the rename so Windows accepts it.

Also smooth the path for crates that hold snapshots but no Module, such as
burn-onnx during codegen:

- Re-export burn_pack from burn-store. The TensorEntry impl only applies for
  the burn-pack version burn-store was built against, so a separate dependency
  resolving elsewhere fails as "TensorSnapshot doesn't implement TensorEntry"
  rather than as a version conflict.
- Replace bridge::tensor_to_snapshot with From<burn_pack::Tensor> for
  TensorSnapshot, matching the TensorEntry impl on the save side.

Covered by a burn-store integration test that drives the writer through the
re-export, so the surface a downstream crate sees is pinned from outside.

* docs(pack): document streaming saves, fix broken bridge doc link

The bridge module header still pointed at tensor_to_snapshot, which the
previous commit replaced with the From<PackTensor> impl. That is a hard
failure: the workspace denies broken_intra_doc_links, so cargo doc
--document-private-items could not document burn-store.

Document what the streaming writer means for users, in the places that
described only the lazy read side:

- burn-pack README gains a TensorEntry sketch and the memory property.
- contributor-book serialization.md said Writer and Reader both operate on
  burn_pack::Tensor, which stopped being true; describe the actual seam.
- burn-book saving-and-loading.md gains a saving counterpart to its
  zero-copy loading section, scoped to file saves since from_bytes builds
  the whole container by definition.
- burn-store README notes streaming saves alongside zero-copy loading.

Also state the two costs of building beside the destination, which the
write_to_file docs claimed the benefit of without the price: overwriting
needs room for a second copy, and a hard kill strands a scratch file.

Minor cleanups: drop the FileSink handle explicitly rather than scoping a
block around it (File is unbuffered, so the flush it replaced was a no-op),
drop ScratchFile::path in favour of the field at its one call site, and
shape the direct_writer test helper like the tensor it builds.

* fix(store): correct quantized data_len, harden the streaming write path

data_len() disagreed with the bytes TensorData actually produces for QFloat,
in two ways: size_bits_stored()/8 divides to zero for Q4/Q2 under
QuantStore::Native, and the QPARAM_ALIGN round-up added padding that
QuantizedBytes::new never inserts. That was harmless while the descriptor
took its length from the materialized bytes, but the streaming writer
reserves space from data_len(), so quantized saves began failing with
TensorBytesSizeMismatch:

  q8 3x3    declared=16  actual=13
  q4 32x32  declared=4   actual=1028

Round the stored width up and drop the padding. The existing test missed
this because 32x32 Q8 is the one case both bugs skip; it now walks Q8/Q4/Q2
against shapes whose value bytes are not a multiple of four. safetensors
feeds the same function into its offsets, so this fixes that latently too.

Write path, all found by review of the streaming change:

- Take per-tensor offsets from planning instead of looking descriptors back
  up by name. The lookup made name() stability an unstated requirement, and
  write_tensors had no branch for an offset that moved backwards, so an
  unstable name() could silently write tensors at the wrong offsets. Reading
  every accessor once during planning removes the requirement entirely.
- Reject a byte_len that contradicts the entry's own shape and dtype while
  planning, before any I/O. Quantized is exempt, which is the honest reason
  byte_len is a trait method rather than something the writer derives.
- sync_all() before the rename. File::flush is a no-op and dropping the
  handle discards what close() reports, yet that is exactly where NFS and
  quota failures surface; without it a truncated container could be renamed
  over a good one while write_to_file returned Ok.
- Name the tensor on a provider failure, and stop reporting a backend panic
  during readback as PackError::IoError. It arrives mid-write alongside the
  writer's own disk errors and read exactly like one.
- Give file errors their operation and path, and hand back the scratch file
  and its guard together so neither can exist without the other.

Docs: the drop-before-rename comment claimed Windows will not rename an open
file, but Rust's File sets FILE_SHARE_DELETE. Also state what replacement by
rename costs (a second copy on disk, permissions and hard links not carried
over, symlinks replaced rather than followed) and that the guarantee covers
process failure rather than power loss.

Tests: pin laziness against the shipped TensorSnapshot path rather than only
a test double, cover the rename-failure branch, and add BurnpackStore file
mode, the adapter save path, and quantized round trips.

* refactor(pack): trim the review-fix commit's plumbing

Cleanups from a review pass over dcc5a3b6c, no behavior change:

- Fold build_metadata into plan. It unpacked one 3-tuple, did eight lines of
  work, and repacked a second differently-shaped 3-tuple for plan to unpack
  again; now only build_descriptors' tuple crosses a function boundary.
- Collapse Error::in_tensor's six identical rewrap arms into one or-pattern
  that annotates the message in place. Still exhaustive, half the length.
- Use Shape::num_elements() and Shape's Display in check_byte_len instead of
  reconstructing both inline (the Display change also drops a temporary Vec
  from the error path).
- debug_assert that placements and tensors agree in length before the zip in
  write_tensors, turning a documented invariant into a checked one.
- Move the quantized round-trip test from burnpack_store.rs (whose charter is
  the BurnpackStore API, which the test never touched) to direct_writer.rs,
  trimmed to one tensor carrying both risk axes: the scheme/shape sweep it
  duplicated already lives in tensor_snapshot.rs at the unit level.

* test(pack): take impl Into<Shape> in the LazyEntry fixture

The constructor took &[usize] and converted by hand, computing the element
count off the slice and Shape::from(to_vec()) two lines later - two views of
the same data that had to agree. Accept impl Into<Shape> (matching
burn_pack::Tensor::new), convert once, and derive the count from the stored
Shape via num_elements(). Call sites drop to bare array literals.

Also explain the values ramp: per-tensor bases keep every tensor's bytes
unique, which the byte-for-byte eager-vs-lazy comparison relies on to catch
swapped or misplaced tensor data.

* fix(pack): enforce sync-before-rename in the type, correct durability docs

Second review pass over the streaming writer. Every finding from the first
pass was verified resolved (including measured quantized layouts confirming
the data_len fix, and that the flex backend's Native store rewrite means the
tests genuinely exercise the div-to-zero path). What it surfaced:

- Nothing enforced FileSink::finish before ScratchFile::persist: forget the
  call and the sink drops, discarding the sync error the mechanism exists to
  catch. persist now consumes the sink and calls finish itself, making the
  ordering unrepresentable at the one call site.
- The two durability doc blocks contradicted each other. write_to_file's
  power-loss caveat predated sync_all and warned about the one ordering that
  can no longer happen; finish claimed to make the rename durable, which
  sync_all does not do (the directory is not synced). Both now tell the same
  story: old container or complete new one, never a mixture, but the rename
  itself may be lost.
- The error-context fixes had no regression tests: deleting the in_tensor
  annotation or reverting the bridge's error classification failed nothing.
  Pinned by a name assertion in the failing-provider test and a new bridge
  test walking IoError and PanicError through the writer.
- Promote the zip-length debug_assert to assert_eq: release-mode truncation
  is a corrupt container, and the guard already turns a panic into a clean
  abort.
- in_tensor no longer annotates TensorNotFound, whose payload is a name, not
  a sentence (it prefixed into "Tensor not found: tensor 'a': b").
- Doc corrections: data_len still listed the alignment padding this branch
  removed; "every accessor is read exactly once" missed that each entry point
  plans anew; "only the producer can compute it" said computability where it
  meant ownership; both quantized test docs now state their dependence on the
  backend's Native-store rewrite; a stale MoveFileExW claim; an em dash.
- New tests: plan-time rejection creates no file at all, and the store's
  auto-extension is exercised by the file-mode round trip (the header claimed
  it; no test used an extensionless path).

* feat(pack): make a successful save durable across power loss on Unix

persist now syncs the destination's parent directory after the rename, so
once write_to_file returns Ok the save survives power loss: previously the
data blocks were synced but the rename itself could be lost, silently
reverting the destination to the old container. If that final sync fails the
error says the container is saved and intact with only durability
unconfirmed, since the generic rename error would wrongly imply the save
did not happen. Windows has no portable directory sync; the docs scope the
guarantee accordingly.

Also pin the plan-time QFloat exemption with an explicit burn-pack test: a
quantized byte_len that shape arithmetic would reject must be accepted,
which previously held only implicitly through a burn-store round trip. The
LazyEntry fixture gains a dtype field to express it.

* fix(store): compute packed quantized sizes per line, open scratch exclusively

Review feedback on #5349:

- data_len took div_ceil over the flattened element count, but packed storage
  is dimension-local: each line along the packed (last) dimension packs into
  whole storage elements on its own, so a non-divisible extent pads per line.
  A [3, 3] Q4 PackedU32 tensor occupies 12 value bytes, not ceil(9/8)*4 = 8.
  No current backend can materialize such a tensor (cubecl rejects the shape
  at allocation, the test backend rewrites packed schemes to Native), so the
  flat formula agreed everywhere reachable; the per-line formula mirrors the
  allocation code and stays correct if that restriction lifts. Pinned by a
  hand-computed formula test, since to_data() cannot produce a comparison.

- ScratchFile opened its scratch path with File::create, which follows an
  existing symlink and truncates its target - and the pid+counter name is
  predictable enough to plant one. Open with File::create_new instead, which
  refuses an existing path, and answer AlreadyExists (stale leftover, pid
  reuse, planted link) by moving on to the next counter value.

* refactor(store): hold TensorSnapshot's data_fn in an Arc

Prerequisite for moving the deferred byte source into burn_pack::Tensor.
A deferred Tensor has to stay Send: OptimizerRecord holds Vec<Tensor> and
burn-train's Checkpoint is Send + 'static, so an async checkpointer moves
one across threads. That forces the provider closure to be Send, which in
turn forces the snapshot behind it to be Send.

Nothing about the captured data blocked this: burn tensors are already
Send + Sync, and Rc was simply the default choice. Swap it for
Arc<dyn Fn + Send + Sync> and TensorSnapshot becomes Send + Sync, pinned
by a new test.

The bound is now load-bearing for every data_fn, so a captured Cell no
longer compiles; the one such test counter becomes an AtomicUsize.

* refactor(pack): make deferred bytes a property of Tensor

Per review feedback: burn_pack::Tensor is already the format-level
representation of a tensor, and whether its bytes are resident or produced
on demand belongs to it rather than to a separate writer-input abstraction.
The reader has always handed back tensors whose bytes are read lazily from
the source, so a parallel trait for the write side made the two directions
asymmetric for no reason.

Replace TensorEntry and Writer<T> with a private eager-or-deferred source
inside Tensor. Tensor::new is unchanged; Tensor::deferred takes a byte
length plus a provider that yields the data when the writer reaches it.
Writer goes back to a plain Vec<Tensor>.

This also removes a class of bug rather than defending against it. With a
trait, name() was called once while planning and again while writing, so
nothing guaranteed the two agreed; a plain String field cannot disagree
with itself. Callers lose the Writer::new(vec![]) turbofish and the
per-entry monomorphization at the same time.

The public bytes field moves behind Tensor::into_bytes, which is fallible
because a deferred provider can fail. Reader-produced tensors are always
resident, so record paths that take that route are annotated as infallible
rather than propagating an error that cannot occur.

burn-store converts a TensorSnapshot into a deferred tensor, replacing the
TensorEntry impl; the conversion materializes nothing, and the load-side
From<Tensor> stays as it was.

* fix(store): keep the deferred-tensor refactor building without atomics

The Arc migration broke `thumbv6m-none-eabi`, which xtask builds for every
crate in NO_STD_CRATES: `alloc::sync` does not exist without atomic CAS, so
`use alloc::sync::Arc` failed outright. A blanket sed also rewrote two
deliberate `alloc::rc::Rc::new` sites in the safetensors store, which had
been chosen for exactly that reason.

Make the pointer and its bound follow the target. `Send + Sync` exists so a
snapshot can back a deferred burn_pack::Tensor crossing threads through
burn-train's async checkpointer; a target without atomic CAS has no threads,
so neither the bound nor the atomic pointer is needed or available there.
Both crates now select `Arc` or `Rc` by cfg, and express the closure bound
as a blanket trait (`ByteSource`, `DataSource`) so the constructors keep one
signature. burn-store gains a `DataFn` alias and a `TensorSnapshot::data_fn`
constructor, so callers no longer name the pointer type at all.

Also from review:

- Add `Tensor::bytes(&self)` alongside `into_bytes(self)`. Four call sites
  were cloning the whole tensor, or its name and shape, purely to read
  metadata before consuming it; they now borrow. Drop `is_resident`, whose
  only caller was an assertion already covered behaviourally.
- Retire rationale left behind by the deleted trait: `Placement` no longer
  guards against unstable accessors, `write_tensor_data` no longer avoids a
  per-entry-type monomorphization, and `data_fn` is no longer an `Rc`.
- Note on `Source` that `Bytes` is already lazy about the copy, and that
  `Deferred` defers the call that produces it, so the two are not redundant.

* fix(pack): stop bytes() copying optimizer state, pin the memory bound

Review follow-ups on the deferred-tensor work.

The bytes() accessor added last commit was the wrong choice for the two
optimizer load paths. Bytes::clone only shares when the allocation
controller offers duplicate(); optimizer records carry plain heap buffers
from Tensor::new, so cloning deep-copied every state tensor and then dropped
the original on the next iteration. Both sites go back to hoisting the
metadata and moving the bytes out. The doc oversold the method the same way:
it named only the heap case, missing that a device-backed buffer is copied
too, which forces the whole readback the writer otherwise streams in chunks.

Also:

- Export ByteSource. It appears in Tensor::deferred's signature but sat in a
  private module, so downstreams could neither name it nor follow the link,
  and its rationale was invisible in rendered docs.
- Map error classes in bridge.rs's load direction the way the save direction
  already does. Flattening nine variants into IoError sent readers looking at
  their disk for what was usually a data problem, and survived a round trip.
- Use TensorSnapshot::data_fn at the three adapter.rs sites the constructor
  was added for, which lets adapter.rs drop its own cfg-Arc alias.
- Correct docs that outlived their code: cfg comments claiming a Send + Sync
  bound the cfg below removes, lib.rs using "resident" in the sense the rest
  of the crate uses for its opposite, and a type doc naming one accessor and
  asserting a shape/dtype relation quantized data breaks.

Two test gaps closed. Tensor::bytes had none, and its deferred arm was
reached by nothing, so its contract (borrow, no caching, unannotated
provider errors) is now pinned. And nothing verified the peak-memory
guarantee the feature exists for: streaming_memory.rs counts live heap bytes
with its own allocator and asserts no earlier tensor's payload survives into
the next provider. Confirmed it fails when write_tensors retains the bytes.

* refactor(pack): add Tensor::into_parts, rename bytes to to_bytes

Cleanup pass over the previous commit.

Four reviewers independently landed on the same finding: the Tensor to
TensorData unpack was open-coded at three call sites, each hoisting and
cloning the metadata before consuming the tensor, two of them carrying a
verbatim-identical comment explaining why. The cause was an API gap, since
`source` is private and `into_bytes` consumes the whole value, so no caller
could move the name out and still reach the bytes. `into_parts` hands over
everything in one move, collapsing all three sites and dropping a `String`
allocation per tensor from every record load. It also picks up the site in
burn-core the previous commit missed, which is the evidence that patching
call sites was the wrong depth.

Rename `bytes` to `to_bytes`. The previous commit answered "a caller picked
the wrong accessor and silently got a full copy" with a longer doc; the
crate already follows RFC 430 elsewhere (`Header::into_bytes`,
`Writer::into_bytes`), so `to_` carries that warning at the call site
instead, and the doc shrinks to the two lines a caller needs.

Also: trim a comment in bridge.rs that re-derived its own cross-reference,
inline a single-use test helper, drop assertions the signature already
guarantees, state streaming_memory's file-size guard directly instead of
hiding it in integer division, and forward realloc/alloc_zeroed to System so
that test binary keeps in-place growth and pre-zeroed pages. The unit tests
need atomic CAS for their counters, so the module is now gated on it,
keeping `--tests` compiling for embedded targets.

Re-verified that streaming_memory still fails when the writer retains a
tensor's bytes.

* docs(pack): scope the crash-safety claims to what the primitive gives

Review pointed out that the ScratchFile implementation comment concedes
Windows documents no atomicity guarantee when a rename replaces an existing
file, while write_to_file, both READMEs and the book promised all-or-nothing
replacement with no such limit.

The process-level half was always sound everywhere, and stays stated that
way: the rename is a single call, so it either took effect or it did not,
and a panic or a killed process cannot tear it. What was overstated is the
power-loss half. The old text claimed that off Unix a crash "can revert the
destination to the old container", which asserts the old file survives;
without a documented atomic replace it may not. That now says the contents
are one or the other and does not promise which.

The terse restatements were the unscoped ones. burn-store's README said
saves "land atomically" with no qualifier, and the book's "an interrupted
save" read as covering power loss.

Not taking the other half of the suggestion, a platform-specific atomic
replace via ReplaceFileW: it needs a fallback for a missing destination and
hardens only the system-crash case, on the one platform where the directory
sync that the rest of the guarantee rests on is unavailable anyway. Scoping
the claim is proportionate; if Windows durability is wanted later it should
be its own change.

* refactor(pack): own the length invariant, drop two public traits, split the file writers

Three review points from @laggui.

Source now resolves and validates its own bytes. Only Writer::materialize
checked the provider's output length, so to_bytes, into_bytes and into_parts
all discarded the declared len and handed back whatever the provider gave,
leaving byte_len reporting a number the caller would not get. Every
materialization path goes through one check now, which makes the writer's own
redundant and it is gone.

ByteSource and DataSource were trait aliases in all but name, existing only
because the closure bound varies by target, and both had leaked into public
APIs whose shape changed with the target. Two cfg'd signatures delegating to a
private constructor do the same job with nothing new exported.

write_to_file goes back to writing in place, and the scratch-and-rename
behavior moves to write_to_file_atomic. The mid-write failure it protects
against comes from deferred tensors, and only BurnpackStore has those;
ModuleRecord, OptimizerRecord and LrSchedulerRecord all hold resident bytes
that cannot fail to materialize, yet were paying an fsync of the whole
container per save plus, when overwriting, room for a second copy. Those
callers keep the behavior and the cost they had before. A test pins the
difference so the two methods cannot quietly converge.

* fix(std): divide the packed dimension, not the flattened count, in quantized_data_len

A packed store rounds up only the packed extent and leaves the other
dimensions intact, so a non-divisible extent pads once per line rather than
once over the whole tensor. `CubeTensor::quantized_storage` builds exactly
that shape:

    shape[packed_dim] = shape[packed_dim].div_ceil(scheme.num_quants());

`quantized_data_len` flattened first, which under-counts whenever the packed
extent is not a multiple of `num_quants`: a [3, 3] Q4 `PackedU32` tensor
occupies 3 * ceil(3 / 8) = 3 words, not ceil(9 / 8) = 2.

That was latent while the number only fed safetensors offsets. It is fatal
for a deferred tensor, which declares its length from `data_len()` before the
writer reserves space, so an under-count fails the save outright.

Covered by a formula-level test across a two-dimensional non-divisible shape,
a higher-rank one, and a divisible one that must still agree with the
flattened count. The existing sweep against `to_data()` is unchanged, so the
materializable schemes are still pinned to real bytes.

Restores a test the previous merge dropped. Upstream introduced
`quantized_data_len` and I took it wholesale, concluding that no per-line rule
existed after grepping only burn-std; the rule lives in burn-cubecl, where the
allocation happens.

* docs(pack): point the atomicity caveats at write_to_file_atomic

Splitting the two file writers left four doc references behind. write_into
said write_to_file has no partial-write caveat, which stopped being true when
it went back to writing in place: it has the same caveat, on the destination
rather than on the caller's buffer. ScratchFile and FileSink::finish both
exist only for the atomic path, and Layout is now shared by both writers.

BurnpackStore::collect_from no longer materializes during collection. Paired
with write_to_file, peak host memory is bounded by the largest single tensor
rather than by the whole module.

Closes #5219

* fix(pack): make write_to_file all-or-nothing, ease direct writer use

Lazy TensorEntry providers run during the write, so "the provider failed" and
"the provider's bytes did not match its declared length" are now ordinary
outcomes rather than disk errors. write_to_file created the destination up
front, leaving a truncated container there on any such failure - and clobbering
a valid file that was already at that path.

Build into a scratch sibling of the destination and rename it into place only
once the container is complete. A sibling rather than a temp dir keeps the
rename on one filesystem. An RAII guard removes the scratch file on any early
return, and the handle is closed before the rename so Windows accepts it.

Also smooth the path for crates that hold snapshots but no Module, such as
burn-onnx during codegen:

- Re-export burn_pack from burn-store. The TensorEntry impl only applies for
  the burn-pack version burn-store was built against, so a separate dependency
  resolving elsewhere fails as "TensorSnapshot doesn't implement TensorEntry"
  rather than as a version conflict.
- Replace bridge::tensor_to_snapshot with From<burn_pack::Tensor> for
  TensorSnapshot, matching the TensorEntry impl on the save side.

Covered by a burn-store integration test that drives the writer through the
re-export, so the surface a downstream crate sees is pinned from outside.

* docs(pack): document streaming saves, fix broken bridge doc link

The bridge module header still pointed at tensor_to_snapshot, which the
previous commit replaced with the From<PackTensor> impl. That is a hard
failure: the workspace denies broken_intra_doc_links, so cargo doc
--document-private-items could not document burn-store.

Document what the streaming writer means for users, in the places that
described only the lazy read side:

- burn-pack README gains a TensorEntry sketch and the memory property.
- contributor-book serialization.md said Writer and Reader both operate on
  burn_pack::Tensor, which stopped being true; describe the actual seam.
- burn-book saving-and-loading.md gains a saving counterpart to its
  zero-copy loading section, scoped to file saves since from_bytes builds
  the whole container by definition.
- burn-store README notes streaming saves alongside zero-copy loading.

Also state the two costs of building beside the destination, which the
write_to_file docs claimed the benefit of without the price: overwriting
needs room for a second copy, and a hard kill strands a scratch file.

Minor cleanups: drop the FileSink handle explicitly rather than scoping a
block around it (File is unbuffered, so the flush it replaced was a no-op),
drop ScratchFile::path in favour of the field at its one call site, and
shape the direct_writer test helper like the tensor it builds.

* fix(store): correct quantized data_len, harden the streaming write path

data_len() disagreed with the bytes TensorData actually produces for QFloat,
in two ways: size_bits_stored()/8 divides to zero for Q4/Q2 under
QuantStore::Native, and the QPARAM_ALIGN round-up added padding that
QuantizedBytes::new never inserts. That was harmless while the descriptor
took its length from the materialized bytes, but the streaming writer
reserves space from data_len(), so quantized saves began failing with
TensorBytesSizeMismatch:

  q8 3x3    declared=16  actual=13
  q4 32x32  declared=4   actual=1028

Round the stored width up and drop the padding. The existing test missed
this because 32x32 Q8 is the one case both bugs skip; it now walks Q8/Q4/Q2
against shapes whose value bytes are not a multiple of four. safetensors
feeds the same function into its offsets, so this fixes that latently too.

Write path, all found by review of the streaming change:

- Take per-tensor offsets from planning instead of looking descriptors back
  up by name. The lookup made name() stability an unstated requirement, and
  write_tensors had no branch for an offset that moved backwards, so an
  unstable name() could silently write tensors at the wrong offsets. Reading
  every accessor once during planning removes the requirement entirely.
- Reject a byte_len that contradicts the entry's own shape and dtype while
  planning, before any I/O. Quantized is exempt, which is the honest reason
  byte_len is a trait method rather than something the writer derives.
- sync_all() before the rename. File::flush is a no-op and dropping the
  handle discards what close() reports, yet that is exactly where NFS and
  quota failures surface; without it a truncated container could be renamed
  over a good one while write_to_file returned Ok.
- Name the tensor on a provider failure, and stop reporting a backend panic
  during readback as PackError::IoError. It arrives mid-write alongside the
  writer's own disk errors and read exactly like one.
- Give file errors their operation and path, and hand back the scratch file
  and its guard together so neither can exist without the other.

Docs: the drop-before-rename comment claimed Windows will not rename an open
file, but Rust's File sets FILE_SHARE_DELETE. Also state what replacement by
rename costs (a second copy on disk, permissions and hard links not carried
over, symlinks replaced rather than followed) and that the guarantee covers
process failure rather than power loss.

Tests: pin laziness against the shipped TensorSnapshot path rather than only
a test double, cover the rename-failure branch, and add BurnpackStore file
mode, the adapter save path, and quantized round trips.

* refactor(pack): trim the review-fix commit's plumbing

Cleanups from a review pass over dcc5a3b6c, no behavior change:

- Fold build_metadata into plan. It unpacked one 3-tuple, did eight lines of
  work, and repacked a second differently-shaped 3-tuple for plan to unpack
  again; now only build_descriptors' tuple crosses a function boundary.
- Collapse Error::in_tensor's six identical rewrap arms into one or-pattern
  that annotates the message in place. Still exhaustive, half the length.
- Use Shape::num_elements() and Shape's Display in check_byte_len instead of
  reconstructing both inline (the Display change also drops a temporary Vec
  from the error path).
- debug_assert that placements and tensors agree in length before the zip in
  write_tensors, turning a documented invariant into a checked one.
- Move the quantized round-trip test from burnpack_store.rs (whose charter is
  the BurnpackStore API, which the test never touched) to direct_writer.rs,
  trimmed to one tensor carrying both risk axes: the scheme/shape sweep it
  duplicated already lives in tensor_snapshot.rs at the unit level.

* test(pack): take impl Into<Shape> in the LazyEntry fixture

The constructor took &[usize] and converted by hand, computing the element
count off the slice and Shape::from(to_vec()) two lines later - two views of
the same data that had to agree. Accept impl Into<Shape> (matching
burn_pack::Tensor::new), convert once, and derive the count from the stored
Shape via num_elements(). Call sites drop to bare array literals.

Also explain the values ramp: per-tensor bases keep every tensor's bytes
unique, which the byte-for-byte eager-vs-lazy comparison relies on to catch
swapped or misplaced tensor data.

* fix(pack): enforce sync-before-rename in the type, correct durability docs

Second review pass over the streaming writer. Every finding from the first
pass was verified resolved (including measured quantized layouts confirming
the data_len fix, and that the flex backend's Native store rewrite means the
tests genuinely exercise the div-to-zero path). What it surfaced:

- Nothing enforced FileSink::finish before ScratchFile::persist: forget the
  call and the sink drops, discarding the sync error the mechanism exists to
  catch. persist now consumes the sink and calls finish itself, making the
  ordering unrepresentable at the one call site.
- The two durability doc blocks contradicted each other. write_to_file's
  power-loss caveat predated sync_all and warned about the one ordering that
  can no longer happen; finish claimed to make the rename durable, which
  sync_all does not do (the directory is not synced). Both now tell the same
  story: old container or complete new one, never a mixture, but the rename
  itself may be lost.
- The error-context fixes had no regression tests: deleting the in_tensor
  annotation or reverting the bridge's error classification failed nothing.
  Pinned by a name assertion in the failing-provider test and a new bridge
  test walking IoError and PanicError through the writer.
- Promote the zip-length debug_assert to assert_eq: release-mode truncation
  is a corrupt container, and the guard already turns a panic into a clean
  abort.
- in_tensor no longer annotates TensorNotFound, whose payload is a name, not
  a sentence (it prefixed into "Tensor not found: tensor 'a': b").
- Doc corrections: data_len still listed the alignment padding this branch
  removed; "every accessor is read exactly once" missed that each entry point
  plans anew; "only the producer can compute it" said computability where it
  meant ownership; both quantized test docs now state their dependence on the
  backend's Native-store rewrite; a stale MoveFileExW claim; an em dash.
- New tests: plan-time rejection creates no file at all, and the store's
  auto-extension is exercised by the file-mode round trip (the header claimed
  it; no test used an extensionless path).

* feat(pack): make a successful save durable across power loss on Unix

persist now syncs the destination's parent directory after the rename, so
once write_to_file returns Ok the save survives power loss: previously the
data blocks were synced but the rename itself could be lost, silently
reverting the destination to the old container. If that final sync fails the
error says the container is saved and intact with only durability
unconfirmed, since the generic rename error would wrongly imply the save
did not happen. Windows has no portable directory sync; the docs scope the
guarantee accordingly.

Also pin the plan-time QFloat exemption with an explicit burn-pack test: a
quantized byte_len that shape arithmetic would reject must be accepted,
which previously held only implicitly through a burn-store round trip. The
LazyEntry fixture gains a dtype field to express it.

* fix(store): compute packed quantized sizes per line, open scratch exclusively

Review feedback on #5349:

- data_len took div_ceil over the flattened element count, but packed storage
  is dimension-local: each line along the packed (last) dimension packs into
  whole storage elements on its own, so a non-divisible extent pads per line.
  A [3, 3] Q4 PackedU32 tensor occupies 12 value bytes, not ceil(9/8)*4 = 8.
  No current backend can materialize such a tensor (cubecl rejects the shape
  at allocation, the test backend rewrites packed schemes to Native), so the
  flat formula agreed everywhere reachable; the per-line formula mirrors the
  allocation code and stays correct if that restriction lifts. Pinned by a
  hand-computed formula test, since to_data() cannot produce a comparison.

- ScratchFile opened its scratch path with File::create, which follows an
  existing symlink and truncates its target - and the pid+counter name is
  predictable enough to plant one. Open with File::create_new instead, which
  refuses an existing path, and answer AlreadyExists (stale leftover, pid
  reuse, planted link) by moving on to the next counter value.

* refactor(store): hold TensorSnapshot's data_fn in an Arc

Prerequisite for moving the deferred byte source into burn_pack::Tensor.
A deferred Tensor has to stay Send: OptimizerRecord holds Vec<Tensor> and
burn-train's Checkpoint is Send + 'static, so an async checkpointer moves
one across threads. That forces the provider closure to be Send, which in
turn forces the snapshot behind it to be Send.

Nothing about the captured data blocked this: burn tensors are already
Send + Sync, and Rc was simply the default choice. Swap it for
Arc<dyn Fn + Send + Sync> and TensorSnapshot becomes Send + Sync, pinned
by a new test.

The bound is now load-bearing for every data_fn, so a captured Cell no
longer compiles; the one such test counter becomes an AtomicUsize.

* refactor(pack): make deferred bytes a property of Tensor

Per review feedback: burn_pack::Tensor is already the format-level
representation of a tensor, and whether its bytes are resident or produced
on demand belongs to it rather than to a separate writer-input abstraction.
The reader has always handed back tensors whose bytes are read lazily from
the source, so a parallel trait for the write side made the two directions
asymmetric for no reason.

Replace TensorEntry and Writer<T> with a private eager-or-deferred source
inside Tensor. Tensor::new is unchanged; Tensor::deferred takes a byte
length plus a provider that yields the data when the writer reaches it.
Writer goes back to a plain Vec<Tensor>.

This also removes a class of bug rather than defending against it. With a
trait, name() was called once while planning and again while writing, so
nothing guaranteed the two agreed; a plain String field cannot disagree
with itself. Callers lose the Writer::new(vec![]) turbofish and the
per-entry monomorphization at the same time.

The public bytes field moves behind Tensor::into_bytes, which is fallible
because a deferred provider can fail. Reader-produced tensors are always
resident, so record paths that take that route are annotated as infallible
rather than propagating an error that cannot occur.

burn-store converts a TensorSnapshot into a deferred tensor, replacing the
TensorEntry impl; the conversion materializes nothing, and the load-side
From<Tensor> stays as it was.

* fix(store): keep the deferred-tensor refactor building without atomics

The Arc migration broke `thumbv6m-none-eabi`, which xtask builds for every
crate in NO_STD_CRATES: `alloc::sync` does not exist without atomic CAS, so
`use alloc::sync::Arc` failed outright. A blanket sed also rewrote two
deliberate `alloc::rc::Rc::new` sites in the safetensors store, which had
been chosen for exactly that reason.

Make the pointer and its bound follow the target. `Send + Sync` exists so a
snapshot can back a deferred burn_pack::Tensor crossing threads through
burn-train's async checkpointer; a target without atomic CAS has no threads,
so neither the bound nor the atomic pointer is needed or available there.
Both crates now select `Arc` or `Rc` by cfg, and express the closure bound
as a blanket trait (`ByteSource`, `DataSource`) so the constructors keep one
signature. burn-store gains a `DataFn` alias and a `TensorSnapshot::data_fn`
constructor, so callers no longer name the pointer type at all.

Also from review:

- Add `Tensor::bytes(&self)` alongside `into_bytes(self)`. Four call sites
  were cloning the whole tensor, or its name and shape, purely to read
  metadata before consuming it; they now borrow. Drop `is_resident`, whose
  only caller was an assertion already covered behaviourally.
- Retire rationale left behind by the deleted trait: `Placement` no longer
  guards against unstable accessors, `write_tensor_data` no longer avoids a
  per-entry-type monomorphization, and `data_fn` is no longer an `Rc`.
- Note on `Source` that `Bytes` is already lazy about the copy, and that
  `Deferred` defers the call that produces it, so the two are not redundant.

* fix(pack): stop bytes() copying optimizer state, pin the memory bound

Review follow-ups on the deferred-tensor work.

The bytes() accessor added last commit was the wrong choice for the two
optimizer load paths. Bytes::clone only shares when the allocation
controller offers duplicate(); optimizer records carry plain heap buffers
from Tensor::new, so cloning deep-copied every state tensor and then dropped
the original on the next iteration. Both sites go back to hoisting the
metadata and moving the bytes out. The doc oversold the method the same way:
it named only the heap case, missing that a device-backed buffer is copied
too, which forces the whole readback the writer otherwise streams in chunks.

Also:

- Export ByteSource. It appears in Tensor::deferred's signature but sat in a
  private module, so downstreams could neither name it nor follow the link,
  and its rationale was invisible in rendered docs.
- Map error classes in bridge.rs's load direction the way the save direction
  already does. Flattening nine variants into IoError sent readers looking at
  their disk for what was usually a data problem, and survived a round trip.
- Use TensorSnapshot::data_fn at the three adapter.rs sites the constructor
  was added for, which lets adapter.rs drop its own cfg-Arc alias.
- Correct docs that outlived their code: cfg comments claiming a Send + Sync
  bound the cfg below removes, lib.rs using "resident" in the sense the rest
  of the crate uses for its opposite, and a type doc naming one accessor and
  asserting a shape/dtype relation quantized data breaks.

Two test gaps closed. Tensor::bytes had none, and its deferred arm was
reached by nothing, so its contract (borrow, no caching, unannotated
provider errors) is now pinned. And nothing verified the peak-memory
guarantee the feature exists for: streaming_memory.rs counts live heap bytes
with its own allocator and asserts no earlier tensor's payload survives into
the next provider. Confirmed it fails when write_tensors retains the bytes.

* refactor(pack): add Tensor::into_parts, rename bytes to to_bytes

Cleanup pass over the previous commit.

Four reviewers independently landed on the same finding: the Tensor to
TensorData unpack was open-coded at three call sites, each hoisting and
cloning the metadata before consuming the tensor, two of them carrying a
verbatim-identical comment explaining why. The cause was an API gap, since
`source` is private and `into_bytes` consumes the whole value, so no caller
could move the name out and still reach the bytes. `into_parts` hands over
everything in one move, collapsing all three sites and dropping a `String`
allocation per tensor from every record load. It also picks up the site in
burn-core the previous commit missed, which is the evidence that patching
call sites was the wrong depth.

Rename `bytes` to `to_bytes`. The previous commit answered "a caller picked
the wrong accessor and silently got a full copy" with a longer doc; the
crate already follows RFC 430 elsewhere (`Header::into_bytes`,
`Writer::into_bytes`), so `to_` carries that warning at the call site
instead, and the doc shrinks to the two lines a caller needs.

Also: trim a comment in bridge.rs that re-derived its own cross-reference,
inline a single-use test helper, drop assertions the signature already
guarantees, state streaming_memory's file-size guard directly instead of
hiding it in integer division, and forward realloc/alloc_zeroed to System so
that test binary keeps in-place growth and pre-zeroed pages. The unit tests
need atomic CAS for their counters, so the module is now gated on it,
keeping `--tests` compiling for embedded targets.

Re-verified that streaming_memory still fails when the writer retains a
tensor's bytes.

* docs(pack): scope the crash-safety claims to what the primitive gives

Review pointed out that the ScratchFile implementation comment concedes
Windows documents no atomicity guarantee when a rename replaces an existing
file, while write_to_file, both READMEs and the book promised all-or-nothing
replacement with no such limit.

The process-level half was always sound everywhere, and stays stated that
way: the rename is a single call, so it either took effect or it did not,
and a panic or a killed process cannot tear it. What was overstated is the
power-loss half. The old text claimed that off Unix a crash "can revert the
destination to the old container", which asserts the old file survives;
without a documented atomic replace it may not. That now says the contents
are one or the other and does not promise which.

The terse restatements were the unscoped ones. burn-store's README said
saves "land atomically" with no qualifier, and the book's "an interrupted
save" read as covering power loss.

Not taking the other half of the suggestion, a platform-specific atomic
replace via ReplaceFileW: it needs a fallback for a missing destination and
hardens only the system-crash case, on the one platform where the directory
sync that the rest of the guarantee rests on is unavailable anyway. Scoping
the claim is proportionate; if Windows durability is wanted later it should
be its own change.

* refactor(pack): own the length invariant, drop two public traits, split the file writers

Three review points from @laggui.

Source now resolves and validates its own bytes. Only Writer::materialize
checked the provider's output length, so to_bytes, into_bytes and into_parts
all discarded the declared len and handed back whatever the provider gave,
leaving byte_len reporting a number the caller would not get. Every
materialization path goes through one check now, which makes the writer's own
redundant and it is gone.

ByteSource and DataSource were trait aliases in all but name, existing only
because the closure bound varies by target, and both had leaked into public
APIs whose shape changed with the target. Two cfg'd signatures delegating to a
private constructor do the same job with nothing new exported.

write_to_file goes back to writing in place, and the scratch-and-rename
behavior moves to write_to_file_atomic. The mid-write failure it protects
against comes from deferred tensors, and only BurnpackStore has those;
ModuleRecord, OptimizerRecord and LrSchedulerRecord all hold resident bytes
that cannot fail to materialize, yet were paying an fsync of the whole
container per save plus, when overwriting, room for a second copy. Those
callers keep the behavior and the cost they had before. A test pins the
difference so the two methods cannot quietly converge.

* fix(std): divide the packed dimension, not the flattened count, in quantized_data_len

A packed store rounds up only the packed extent and leaves the other
dimensions intact, so a non-divisible extent pads once per line rather than
once over the whole tensor. `CubeTensor::quantized_storage` builds exactly
that shape:

    shape[packed_dim] = shape[packed_dim].div_ceil(scheme.num_quants());

`quantized_data_len` flattened first, which under-counts whenever the packed
extent is not a multiple of `num_quants`: a [3, 3] Q4 `PackedU32` tensor
occupies 3 * ceil(3 / 8) = 3 words, not ceil(9 / 8) = 2.

That was latent while the number only fed safetensors offsets. It is fatal
for a deferred tensor, which declares its length from `data_len()` before the
writer reserves space, so an under-count fails the save outright.

Covered by a formula-level test across a two-dimensional non-divisible shape,
a higher-rank one, and a divisible one that must still agree with the
flattened count. The existing sweep against `to_data()` is unchanged, so the
materializable schemes are still pinned to real bytes.

Restores a test the previous merge dropped. Upstream introduced
`quantized_data_len` and I took it wholesale, concluding that no per-line rule
existed after grepping only burn-std; the rule lives in burn-cubecl, where the
allocation happens.

* docs(pack): point the atomicity caveats at write_to_file_atomic

Splitting the two file writers left four doc references behind. write_into
said write_to_file has no partial-write caveat, which stopped being true when
it went back to writing in place: it has the same caveat, on the destination
rather than on the caller's buffer. ScratchFile and FileSink::finish both
exist only for the atomic path, and Layout is now shared by both writers.
